courses.description: This course provides an overview and applications of health care marketing theories and methods for health care and public health organizations. Graduate level requirements include a 20-page paper describing a marketing plan and the process used to complete it.

courses.title: Innovation & New Product Strategy
courses.description: Formulating and implementing strategy for growth; analyzing and influencing market structure; developing, pricing, testing new entries; managing the portfolio.
courses.requisites: MKTG 500.

courses.title: International Marketing
courses.description: Marketing planning and strategies for foreign environments; cultural, political, economic factors affecting the international marketer, multinational corporation and multinational market groups.
courses.requisites: MKTG 500.

courses.title: Listening to the Voice of the Market
courses.description: Market-oriented ethnography and other qualitative research methods are used to obtain a deeper understanding of consumer wants, needs, behaviors and experiences with brands and markets. The findings can be used to guide managerial decision-making.
courses.requisites: MKTG 500 or MKTG 510.

courses.title: Generative AI for Market Insight and Strategies
courses.description: The course is divided into three modules. In the Algorithms module, we cover the principles of Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs). We discuss the concepts associated with transformers, including the basic building blocks. We also cover the popular transformers (BERT, GPT, and T5). In the Prompt Engineering module, we cover various prompting techniques for optimal content generation such as Chain of Thought, RGC, and Reverse prompting, among others. In the Applications and Strategic considerations of Generative AI module, we apply prompting to a real-world business scenario. Moreover, we cover topics such as Generative AI and innovation, customer support, and review mining.

courses.title: Marketing Research For Managers
courses.description: Specification of management information needs, evaluation of research proposals and findings, methods of gathering and analyzing data, administrative aspects of research and decisions.
courses.requisites: MKTG 500.

courses.title: Marketing Research for Managers
courses.description: Whether a firm is consumer, business or service-oriented, acquiring and using information is critical for business planning and decisions. Thus, this course is appropriate for anyone who relies on data in their decision making, whether the context is entrepreneurial, not-for profit, public health, or marketing. This course is designed to provide an overview of applied research methods as used in marketing research and as tools to help make effective marketing decisions. The course is for managers who will be using marketing data rather than those doing \"marketing research.\" The course emphasizes the analysis and interpretation of market research data for marketing/managerial decision making, and the design of research studies so that the results are both meaningful and valid. Towards this end, we will examine exploratory research (including projective techniques and focus groups), descriptive research (including cross-sectional and longitudinal survey research), and causal research (including experimentation and test marketing). The course will cover common areas of application. The focus is on helping the manager become a better consumer of market research data through an improved understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of various research methods as well as a basic understanding of data analysis.

courses.title: Marketing of Innovation
courses.description: Explores concepts and best practices for bringing very new technologies and innovations to the marketplace. Uses team projects based in the sciences (e.g., biotech, optics, IT) to assess market opportunities and create strategies for commercialization.
courses.requisites: MKTG 510.

courses.title: Marketing of Innovations
courses.description: This course provides a market-based view of innovation and entrepreneurial activities. The focus is on how to apply an effective process to identify new product and entrepreneurial opportunities, and to develop an appropriate plan to bring the product to market. We will cover topics such as the emergence of innovative ideas, new product development within and beyond organizational boundaries, innovation in an entrepreneurial environment, and marketing strategies for innovations.
courses.requisites: MKTG 510

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Qualified students working on an individual basis with professors who have agreed to supervise such work. Graduate students doing independent work which cannot be classified as actual research will register for credit under course number 599, 699, or 799.

courses.title: Academic Writing & Presenting
courses.description: This PhD seminar will teach students how to communicate. Specifically, students will learn how to present and write so that other scholars will understand and be interested in their research.

courses.title: Marketing Research Methods 1: Constructs and Measurement
courses.description: The primary purpose of this seminar is to introduce doctoral students in marketing and related disciplines to defining constructs which are fundamental to testing theories and relationships and to issues revolving around the measurement of constructs. These are two of the most fundamental components of empirical research in the social sciences. The course will focus on defining constructs as well as the key components in the measurement of those constructs including reliability, convergent, and discriminant validity. We will also cover the concepts of internal and external validity as well as potential threats to the valid measurement of constructs.

courses.title: Research Methods 2 - Experimental Design
courses.description: This seminar will discuss topics related to conducting experimental research: idea generation, experimental design, analyzing data, and reporting and presenting experimental research. This is primarily a skills-building class, and thus offers a practical, learning-by-doing approach.

courses.title: Research Methods In Marketing
courses.description: This course will introduce students to testing theories and relationships with the development of constructs and addressing issues revolving around the measurement of such constructs - two of the most fundamental and classic components of empirical research in the social sciences. In addition, this course will explore the key issues related to conducting the broad variety of research methods used in marketing including lab experiments, field and natural experiments, survey research, secondary data analysis, and qualitative research. By the end of the course, students should be able to use fundamental research concepts gained in the course to design and evaluate research in marketing.

courses.title: Marketing Theory and Conceptual Foundations 1
courses.description: This course is a doctoral seminar with the goal to lay the student's conceptual foundations surrounding topics in scholarly marketing research. This course is intended for students with a wide variety of interests and backgrounds, and will apply the \"Tell-Show-Do\" technique to give both a conceptual and an applied experience in using the course materials for thoughtfully and successfully conducting scholarly marketing research. The first part will be lectures and adjacent discussions in which I will highlight and review course topics. Reading the assigned materials prior to class and active involvement during the lecture will increase the value students gain from the course, as well as make it more interesting for everyone. The second part will be written assignments through which students will apply learnings from the lectures to actual scholarly marketing research problems. Similar to the expectations in other courses, preparation is paramount to making the in-class activities and our associated in-class discussions valuable.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Marketing Theory 2
courses.description: This class is the second part of the doctoral seminar in marketing theory. We will systematically examine one of the most critical factors that drive successful research, conceptualization. As MacInnis (2011) defines it, \"conceptualization is a process of abstract thinking, involving the mental representation of an idea\" (p. 140). Conceptualization is closely related to the theoretical strength of a research paper. Conceptual contribution is often used interchangeably with theoretical contribution.

courses.title: Consumer Psychology
courses.description: This PhD seminar will introduce students to academic research in consumer psychology. In seven weeks, we will read, discuss, and evaluate articles published in marketing, psychology, and the social sciences.

courses.title: Consumer Behavior Foundations
courses.description: This PhD seminar will introduce students to academic research in consumer behavior. We will read, discuss, and evaluate articles in marketing, psychology, and the social sciences that investigate the psychological and cultural forces that shape how people desire, search for, buy, use, and dispose of products and services in the marketplace.

courses.title: Consumer Behavior Special Topics 1: Information Processing
courses.description: This seminar covers extant work in the fields of consumer research, psychology, and other related fields to provide a working knowledge of theoretical and methodological issues in studying automatic and perceptual influences on consumer judgment and choice.

courses.title: Consumer Behavior Special Topics 2: Decision Making
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to provide Ph.D.-level coverage of the psychology of decision making and application of behavioral decision principles in marketing context. Although the normative issue of how decisions should be made is relevant, the descriptive issue of how decisions are made is the main focus of the course.

courses.title: Socio-Cultural Aspects of Markets and Consumer Behavior
courses.description: This course exposes students to the foundations of Consumer Culture Theory (CCT) and overviews research that is based on a humanistic, sociological, and/or cultural anthropological perspective on markets and consumer behavior. Based on a series of readings, students will acquire the necessary skills and abilities to ask relevant and interesting research questions in this tradition while being invited to challenge existing theories and findings.

courses.title: Marketing Management and Strategy
courses.description: The primary purpose of this seminar is to introduce doctoral students in marketing and related disciplines with a broad foundation of the issues and literature in various key theories and models with asymmetric information. These models are key to the design of marketing strategies. More specifically, we will focus on the most prominent theories/models that cover these issues including Principal-Agent models (also called Agency Theory), Multi-Tasking models (a key extension of the Principal-Agent models), and Signaling and Adverse Selection models. Collectively, they cover a broad range of issues of relevance to the field of marketing, corporate finance, economics, organization behavior, accounting, and entrepreneurship and as such have been a cornerstone of a large body of research and teaching in the business schools.

courses.title: Marketing Strategy
courses.description: This seminar provides doctoral students with a broad foundation on organizational design - both within and between organizations and its implications for and interactions with strategic marketing decisions. The seminar will cover both classics and recent research in the field and is intended to provide a working knowledge of the theoretical and methodological issues in substantive topics focusing on channels, business-to-business marketing, strategic alliances, Salesforce design and compensation, branding, and marketing strategy.

courses.title: Doctoral Seminar in Marketing Strategy 2
courses.description: This class is the second part of the doctoral seminar in marketing methods. It is intended to be an introduction to the substantive literature in marketing strategy which investigate research questions at many interesting levels of analysis, including the individual, dyad, group, firm, inter-organizational, and industry level. This course exposes doctoral students to a variety of research designs and techniques, including laboratory and field surveys, experiments, quasi-experiments, qualitative and secondary data.

courses.title: Quantitative Marketing Research 1
courses.description: In this seminar we will focus on causal models from observational data. Physical randomization with experiments are one of the cleanest ways to build causal models. However physical randomization - either through a lab experiment or a field experiment - is not always feasible. Often times we are restricted to delineate causal effects from observational and secondary data. This seminar will cover foundational elements of modern practices of causal inference using observational data. We will cover potential outcomes model as well as discuss in detail the most common designs: sub-classification and propensity score, regression discontinuity, instrumental variables and difference in differences.

courses.title: Marketing Models
courses.description: This course will introduce and acquaint students with theoretical (a.k.a. analytical) models in marketing and how causal models can be estimated from observational data.

courses.title: Quantitative Marketing Research 2
courses.description: The purpose of this seminar is to review and discuss quantitative models (both analytical and empirical) in marketing research. We will survey selected economic modeling applications that address substantive phenomena or issues related to marketing. While covering the general issues, our discussion will also pay attention to current or emerging issues in digital markets. The main materials are selected papers in marketing, economics and other academic fields.

courses.title: Advanced Consumer Behavior Research
courses.description: Advanced theoretical and empirical approaches to investigating consumer behavior in scholarly research.

courses.title: Experimental Research Methods in Marketing
courses.description: Statistical, methodological and interpretive issues in the design of laboratory and field experiments/quasi-experiments for marketing and consumer research.
courses.requisites: MKTG 500.

courses.title: Marketing Colloquium
courses.description: This colloquium covers diverse special topics in current marketing research. The topics are chosen to utilize the research strengths of the participating faculty and to complement the doctoral students' current course of study.

courses.title: Special Topics in Marketing
courses.description: The Special Topics in Marketing Research seminars present the issues, methods, findings, and implications for a variety of research areas in marketing. Depending on the particular semester, this course could focus on selected topics in consumer psychology, consumer culture theory, marketing strategy, or marketing models. Please contact the faculty instructor listed on the course for more details.

courses.description: The development and exchange of scholarly information, usually in a small group setting. The scope of work shall consist of research by course registrants, with the exchange of the results of such research through discussion, reports, and/or papers.

courses.description: The development and exchange of scholarly information, usually in a small group setting. The scope of work shall consist of research by course registrants, with the exchange of the results of such research through discussion, reports, and/or papers.
courses.requisites: MKTG 696A.

courses.title: Marketing Management and Strategy
courses.description: The development and exchange of scholarly information, usually in a small group setting. The scope of work shall consist of research by course registrants, with the exchange of the results of such research through discussion, reports, and/or papers.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Consumer Behavior
courses.description: Doctoral seminar focusing on the psychological aspects of consumer behavior. Topics to include information processing, attitude formation, perception, decision making, persuasion, and motivation.
courses.requisites: Admission to marketing graduate program or consent of department.

courses.title: Marketing Models

courses.title: Special Topics in Entrepreneurship
courses.description: The development and exchange of scholarly information, usually in a small group setting. The scope of the work shall include the advanced exploration of current topics in entrepreneurship, which will require course registrants to engage in research and scholarly exchanges through class discussion, reports, and/or papers. Course may include special topics in entrepreneurship such as the marketing of innovations and early stage technologies, the entrepreneurial dimensions of colleges and universities, intellectual property protection and management, and other potential new topics. Grading scales will be determined on a topic by topic basis, but will include a minimum of one comprehensive exam or one comprehensive term paper/research project.

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Qualified students working on an individual basis with professors who have agreed to supervise such work. Graduate students doing independent work which cannot be classified as actual research will register for credit under course number 599, 699, or 799.

courses.title: Research
courses.description: Individual research, not related to thesis or dissertation preparation, by graduate students.

courses.title: Master's Report
courses.description: Individual study or special project or formal report thereof submitted in lieu of thesis for certain master's degrees.

courses.title: Dissertation
courses.description: Research for the doctoral dissertation (whether library research, laboratory or field observation or research, artistic creation, or dissertation writing).

courses.title: Basic Operations Management
courses.description: OM is concerned with the creation of goods and/services. Topics include business processes, MRP, forecasting, facility planning and layout, inventory management, quality control and just-in-time manufacturing.
courses.requisites: MATH 115A, MATH 115B, and MGMT 276.

courses.title: Managing for Quality Improvement
courses.description: Operational aspect of quality improvement. Topics include statistical process control, quality management programs..

courses.title: Optimization and Decision Support Modeling for Business
courses.description: Decision Support Systems can be defined as 'computer based systems that use data and quantitative models to solve problems and to help managers make decisions.' This is a course on making quantitative decisions. The course introduces the student to optimization methods (linear, integer, nonlinear programming and network models) used in business, decision support via Monte Carlo simulation, and decision making under uncertainty/risk. These concepts are studied in the context of applications in strategic planning, operations/supply chain management, information systems, and other areas of business. Spreadsheets are intuitive and user-friendly platforms for organizing information. Hence, spreadsheets have become indispensable tools of modern business analysis. This course focuses on structuring, analyzing, and solving managerial decision problems using Excel spreadsheets. Specifically, we address problems from operations management (e.g., resource allocation, revenue management, transportation and logistics, outsourcing production) and information systems (e.g., advertising response, media selection model), along with and several other business problems from finance and marketing. In each area, we consider specific managerial decision problems, model them on Excel spreadsheets, analyze and solve the models, and then interpret the solutions obtained. As an added benefit of this course, we will learn to use advanced features of Excel. This includes some of the built-in functions, named ranges, pivot tables, charts, conditional formatting, and some simple macros.

courses.title: Manufacturing Operations Management
courses.description: Operations is a broad scope word used to describe many things within a company. This course is designed to provide students with an in-depth look specifically at selected production operations topics. Topics Include operations strategy, product design for manufacturing, process design, forecasting, aggregate sales and operations planning, capacity management, Materials Resource Planning, production scheduling, and lean/quality principles used in production. Coursework will explore both the quantitative and qualitative techniques that are available to contemporary business managers.

courses.title: Service Operations Management
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with an in-depth look specifically at selected service operations topics; activities entailed in selecting, designing, operating, controlling, and updating service systems.

courses.title: The Supply Chain and Logistics
courses.description: Organization, management and control of material flow processes; logistical strategies and relationships of procurement, handling, warehousing, transportation, and inventory control.
